newsitem.title: USA: Human service firms could be investment-grade - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Human service firms could be investment-grade - S&P.

text.p: Some human services providers have resources available that would contribute to investment-grade ratings, Standard & Poor's Corp said Monday.
"At first glance, human service providers may not appear as strong candidates for investment-grade credit ratings," the agency said in Monday's edition of CreditWeek Municipal.
"However, the essentiality of these services and the strong relationships the providers have with federal, state and local funding agencies can be factors contributing to an investment-grade rating."
Medicaid reform is a key challenge facing human services providers, which offer services like residential living, day treatment, and employment for clients with developmental disabilities, S&P said.

The agency noted that regardless of how Medicaid is ultimately reformed, the goal is to cut costs. That calls into question the profitability of all but the most essential of human services providers.
"However, even entities providing essential services to the most profoundly disabled clients will find it difficult to maintain profitability in an atmosphere of reduced payments," the agency said.
